The kernel follows the same structure as the verified max-reduction example — one thread per output element, serial scan over the reduction dimension, FP32 accumulation for the sum, then a final divide by `dim1` to get the mean. Since the reduction dimension (4096) maps well to coalesced per-warp reads, the simple per-thread approach outperforms fancier warp-shuffle and shared-memory variants I tried along the way. Sometimes the straightforward thing is the right thing.
